signals.title: NOK/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme + Crude Shock
signals.text: NOK leads the G10 currency board with a 1W average gain of +1.753% across 2 pairs, while USD lags at -0.957% across 9 pairs, opening a 2.710% leader-to-laggard spread that clears the threshold for a major bilateral theme. Middle East escalation headlines and Brent testing $120 resistance provide direct terms-of-trade support to the krone, reinforcing Norges Bank restrictive policy where the 4.5% policy rate sits against 2.68% inflation expectations for an authoritative real rate of +1.82%. In contrast, US 5Y yields have fallen 13bp over 5 sessions, led entirely by real yields falling 25bp, weakening nominal dollar support. Technical structure shows USD/NOK in an active downtrend at 9.316, trading below its SMA20 of 9.503 and SMA200 of 9.514, though stretched 2.38 ATR below its 20-day average. Retail sentiment data retail sentiment shows a 100% long extreme on USD/NOK, setting up severe contrarian liquidation risk into any further dollar softness. Trade bias: Bearish USD/NOK, contrarian to extreme retail long positioning. Catalyst: Norges Bank policy meeting 5 Nov. Risk: De-escalation in Middle East shipping disruption sends Brent sharply below $100.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Spec Short + Elevated Vol Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1218, holding below its downward-sloping SMA20 of 1.1238 and SMA50 of 1.1440. CFTC positioning shows leveraged funds heavily net short EUR at -94,138 contracts, placing net exposure in the 2nd percentile of its 52-week range with a z-score of -1.72 after expanding shorts by 35,333 contracts over 4 weeks. Concurrently, options markets show 1M ATM implied volatility at 6.7% versus HV30 of 4.1%, generating an elevated vol risk premium of +2.5% that reflects significant hedging activity over realized price action. The SOFR-to-€STR differential of +146bp continues to structurally favor the dollar, limiting EUR/USD upside into the 1.1240 technical cluster. Trade bias: Neutral/bearish EUR/USD, constrained by policy carry advantage. Catalyst: ECB policy meeting 29 Oct. Risk: Leveraged funds trigger a short squeeze above 1.1240 on any dovish recalibration from the FOMC.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Technical Resistance vs Policy Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7039, staging an intraday bounce above its SMA20 of 0.6980 while encountering stiff overhead resistance near the downward-sloping SMA200 of 0.7054 and SMA50 of 0.7078. Macro policy drivers favor the Australian dollar, with the RBA policy rate at 4.60% against the Fed at 4.00%, creating a -70bp OIS carry advantage in favor of AUD via AONIA 4.60% versus SOFR 3.90%. CFTC leveraged positioning sits long +47,606 contracts in the 62nd percentile of its 52-week range, reflecting steady participation without extreme crowding. Options markets reflect caution, with the 25-delta risk reversal indicating a moderate base put skew of -0.96. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD on carry support, capped by resistance at 0.7055/0.7080. Catalyst: RBA policy decision 3 Nov. Risk: Rejection at the SMA200 of 0.7054 sends spot back down toward the 0.6980 moving average base.
